VCS_VMR0017_v1.0.plain: Verra's revised methodology for grid-connected renewable power. It reopened Verra to solar and wind projects in India.

points.text: Solar PV, onshore and offshore wind and geothermal qualify in low-, lower-middle- and upper-middle-income countries. India is lower-middle income, so these qualify here; hydro is limited to least developed countries.

source.quote: Low-, lower middle- , upper middle- income countries only

points.text: All other conditions of the CDM parent ACM0002 still apply: the plant must be grid-connected, and new or upgraded plants must meet the reference-period and storage rules.

source.quote: This methodology applies to grid-connected renewable energy generation project activities that include

points.text: You must show regulatory surplus (the project is not required by law), plus an investment analysis and common-practice test.

source.quote: Regulatory surplus must be demonstrated in accordance with the rules and requirements regarding regulatory surplus

CCTS_BMEN01.001_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) methodology for grid-connected renewable power, adapted from CDM ACM0002.

points.text: Standalone grid-connected solar and onshore wind plants are excluded. They qualify only as hybrids with battery or pumped storage.

source.quote: Install a Greenfield power plant (excluding standalone grid-connected wind and solar power plants)

points.text: Battery storage is allowed with any new plant, but with upgrades of existing plants only for solar PV or wind.

source.quote: Combinations of renewable energy technologies and mode of BESS applicable for integration

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism; companies with CCTS emission-intensity targets cannot.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity

VCS_VMR0016_v1.0.plain: Verra's revised landfill gas methodology. It replaces ACM0001 and AMS-III.G for new Verra projects from 1 Dec 2026.

points.text: It applies every condition of the CDM parent ACM0001: the gas is flared or used for power, heat or gas supply, and landfill management must not be changed to make more gas.

source.quote: Flare the LFG and/or use the captured LFG in any (combination) of the following ways

points.text: Small projects (power up to 10 MW, heat use, or flaring with carbon credits as the only income) can use a simpler positive list instead of an investment analysis.

source.quote: landfill gas use for electricity generation with a total installed generation capacity that does not exceed 10 MW

points.text: You must show regulatory surplus: the project is not required by law.

source.quote: Where the project proponent demonstrates regulatory surplu s, proceed to Section 7.1.2. Otherwise, the project activity is not additional.

VCS_ACM0001_v19.plain: The CDM landfill gas methodology used under Verra. It is inactive for new Verra projects from 1 Dec 2026 (use VMR0016).

points.text: The project either installs a new gas capture system or upgrades one whose gas was only vented or flared.

source.quote: The captured LFG was vented or flared and not used prior to the implementation of the project activity

points.text: The gas can be flared, or used for electricity, heat, the gas network, trucks or a pipeline.

source.quote: Flare the LFG and/or use the captured LFG in any (combination) of the following ways

points.text: It cannot be used if landfill management is deliberately changed to increase methane.

source.quote: If the management of the SWDS in the project activity is deliberately changed during the crediting in order to in crease methane generation

GS_A6.4-AMM-001_v01.0.plain: Gold Standard's use of the Paris Agreement (Article 6.4) landfill gas methodology, required for new GS landfill projects.

points.text: The gas must be collected only for flaring, power, heat, biomethane, trucks or a dedicated pipeline. Under Gold Standard, flaring alone is not enough: at least one energy use is needed.

source.quote: collect the LFG under the Article 6.4 activity exclusively for one or more of the following applications

points.text: Upgrades qualify only where the captured gas was flared and not used before.

source.quote: where the captured LFG prior to the implementation of the Article 6.4 activity was flared and not used

points.text: The project must not reduce organic waste that would otherwise be recycled.

source.quote: The mechanism methodology is only applicable if the project does not reduce the amount of organic waste that would be recycled in the absence of the Article 6.4 activity

CCTS_BMWA03.002_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) landfill gas methodology for larger projects, adapted from CDM ACM0001.

points.text: The gas can be flared or used for power, heat, the gas network, trucks or a pipeline.

source.quote: Flare the LFG and/or use the captured LFG in any (combination) of the following ways

points.text: Before the project, the landfill gas must have been released, or flared only to meet rules, contracts, safety or odour concerns.

source.quote: Atmospheric release of the LFG or capture of LFG and destruction through flaring to comply with regulations or contractual requirements

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity

CCTS_BMWA03.001_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) landfill gas methodology for small projects, adapted from CDM AMS-III.G.

points.text: It covers capturing and burning methane from landfills.

source.quote: This methodology comprises measures to capture and combust methane from landfills

points.text: It does not apply if the landfill is deliberately managed to produce more methane.

source.quote: This methodology is not applicable if the management of the solid waste disposal site (SWDS) in the project activity is deliberately changed in order to increase methane generation

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity

VCS_AMS-III.D_v22.plain: Small-scale CDM methodology (used under Verra) for capturing methane from manure in farm or central digesters.

points.text: Animals must be kept confined, and manure must not be discharged into rivers or other water.

source.quote: The livestock population in the farm is managed under confined conditions

points.text: Manure must currently sit in an anaerobic system (lagoon or slurry store) for more than 12 months, so dung cakes, solid storage or daily spreading do not qualify.

source.quote: the retention time of manure in the anaerobic management system is greater than 12 months

points.text: Emission reductions are limited to 60,000 t CO2e a year.

source.quote: Measures are limited to those that result in aggregate emission reductions of less than or equal to 60 kt CO2 equivalent annually

VCS_ACM0010_v9.plain: Large-scale CDM methodology (used under Verra) for replacing anaerobic manure systems such as open lagoons with lower-emission systems.

points.text: It applies where an existing anaerobic manure system (open lagoon, slurry pit) is replaced. A new (greenfield) facility qualifies only if its baseline would be an uncovered anaerobic lagoon (p.9 para 16).

source.quote: where the existing anaerobic manure treatment system is replaced by new] animal waste management systems

points.text: If the current system is an uncovered lagoon, manure must stay there for at least 12 months.

source.quote: the retention time of the manure in the system should be at least 12 months

points.text: Co-digestion with other organic waste is not allowed.

source.quote: does not involve co-digestion of manure with other organic wastes

GS_AWMS_v2.0.plain: Gold Standard's Paris-aligned methodology for manure biogas at households, small farms and institutions, used for cooking or heating.

points.text: The manure must currently be handled in a way that rots without air (lagoons, liquid slurry, deep pits); solid storage and dry heaps generally don't qualify.

source.quote: The methodology applies only to livestock manure managed under baseline conditions in systems that result in substantial anaerobic decomposition and methane generation

points.text: Biogas used for cooking or heating is credited here; electricity or mechanical use is allowed only if another approved methodology quantifies it.

source.quote: captured biogas shall be utilised for thermal energy applications

points.text: Each thermal unit credited here must deliver less than 150 kW of heat.

source.quote: the continuous useful energy output shall be less than 150kW thermal per unit

CCTS_BMAG04.001_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) methodology for household and small-farm biogas digesters.

points.text: Digesters must be at individual households or small farms; there is no CCTS route for large or central digesters today.

source.quote: The domestic biogas digester, methane recovery and combustion systems are installed at individual households or small farms

points.text: Credits only count the share of manure that would otherwise rot without air, so dung cakes or solid storage earn little.

source.quote: This methodology is applicable only to the fraction of the manure which would decay anaerobically in the absence of the project activity

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity

VCS_VM0047_v1.1.plain: Verra's methodology for afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR). It uses a dynamic performance benchmark and is CCP-approved.

points.text: Land that was managed forest at any time in the 10 years before the start is excluded under the area-based approach.

source.quote: The project occurs on lands that have met the definition of managed forest at any point in the 10-year period immediately preceding the project start date

points.text: Clearing existing trees must not involve timber harvesting or degrade native ecosystems.

source.quote: Clearing of pre-existing woody biomass involves timber harvesting or results in degradation of native ecosystems

points.text: On wetlands or organic soils, ARR must be combined with a wetland restoration methodology.

source.quote: Where projects take place on organic soils or wetlands, ARR activities are developed using a multiple project activity design

VCS_VM0033_v2.1.plain: Verra's methodology for tidal wetland and seagrass restoration, which covers mangrove restoration.

points.text: Projects that restore tidal wetlands, including mangroves, are eligible.

source.quote: Project activities which restore tidal wetlands (including seagrass meadows, per this methodology’s definition of tidal w etland) are eligible.

points.text: No fertilizer or manure may be applied during the crediting period.

source.quote: Nitrogen fertilizer(s), such as chemical fertilizer or manure, are applied in the project area during the project crediting period

points.text: The project must not lower the water table (reconnecting tidal flow is fine).

source.quote: Project activities lower the water table

CCTS_BMFR05.002_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) methodology for afforestation and reforestation of land that is not wetland.

points.text: Wetland land is excluded; mangroves use BM FR05.001 instead.

source.quote: The land subject to the project activity does not fall in wetland category

points.text: On managed land or organic soils, soil disturbance such as ploughing or digging pits must stay within 10% of the area.

source.quote: Soil disturbance attributable to the project activity does not cover more than 10 per cent of area

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity

CCTS_BMFR05.001_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) methodology for restoring degraded mangrove habitats.

points.text: The land must be degraded mangrove habitat.

source.quote: The land subject to the project activity is degraded mangrove habitat

points.text: More than 90% of the area must be planted with mangrove species, or else site hydrology must not be altered.

source.quote: More than 90 per cent of the project area under the project scenario is planted with mangrove species.

points.text: Soil disturbance must stay within 10% of the area.

source.quote: Soil disturbance attributable to the A/R Indian Carbon Market (ICM) project activity does not cover more than 10 per cent of area.

VCS_AMS-II.D_v13.plain: Small-scale CDM methodology (used under Verra) for energy efficiency, with any fuel switching only as part of it, at industrial facilities.

points.text: Projects that earn credits mainly by switching fuel must use other methodologies.

source.quote: The project activities that aim to earn emission reductions credit primarily through fuel switching

points.text: Electricity savings are capped at 60 GWh a year.

source.quote: may not exceed the equivalent of 60 GWh e per year for electr icity based energy efficient technologies

points.text: Under Verra's rules, switching from coal or oil to natural gas is allowed only in least developed countries, so not in India.

source.quote: Activities that involve switching from a higher to a lower carbon content fossil fuel to generate electricity and/or thermal energy

VCS_AMS-I.C_v22.plain: Small-scale CDM methodology (used under Verra) for renewable heat, such as solar thermal or renewable biomass, that replaces fossil fuel.

points.text: It covers renewable energy that supplies heat and displaces fossil fuel use.

source.quote: This methodology comprises renewable energy technologies that supply users i.e. residential, industrial or commercial facilities with thermal energy that displaces fossil fuel use

points.text: Total heat capacity is capped at 45 MW thermal.

source.quote: The total installed/rated thermal energy generation capacity of the project equipment is equal to or less than 45 MW thermal

points.text: Under Verra's rules, industrial heat from crop-residue or forest-residue biomass is allowed only in least developed countries, so not in India; biogas and dedicated plantation biomass are not restricted.

source.quote: Generating electricity and/or thermal energy for industrial use from the combustion of non-renewable biomass, agro-residue biomass, or forest residue biomass

CCTS_BMIN02.001_v1.0.plain: India's domestic (CCTS) methodology for industrial energy efficiency (efficient motors, pumps, boilers), adapted from CDM AMS-II.D.

points.text: It covers energy-efficiency measures at industrial, mining or mineral production facilities, with no 60 GWh size cap.

source.quote: This methodology comprises any energy efficiency improvement measures implemented at a single or several industrial or mining and mineral production facilities

points.text: Savings that come only from better maintenance do not count.

source.quote: The project activity that aims to achieve energy savings through improved maintenance practices

points.text: Only non-obligated entities can use the offset mechanism; obligated companies cannot.

source.quote: It shall be the responsibility of the non-obligated entity
